inspiration.observed_pattern: An UPDATE JOIN consumes a nested derived source whose grouped inner query uses HAVING to select duplicate keys.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reduced to one duplicate tenant label and one untouched label while retaining the nested derived UPDATE JOIN, aggregate alias in HAVING, and deterministic final state.

fixture_notes: Only the duplicate alpha group qualifies, so catalog row 601 is repaired and row 602 remains unchanged.
determinism_notes: Two fixed catalog rows and two fixed observation groups produce one deterministic mutation. No clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent schedules are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE catalog_rows_min (catalog_id INT PRIMARY KEY, tenant_id INT NOT NULL, label VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL, repaired_label VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL)
CREATE TABLE label_observations_min (observation_id INT PRIMARY KEY, tenant_id INT NOT NULL, label VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL)

steps.sql: UPDATE catalog_rows_min AS r JOIN (SELECT c.catalog_id, c.label FROM catalog_rows_min AS c JOIN (SELECT tenant_id, label, COUNT(*) AS duplicate_count FROM label_observations_min GROUP BY tenant_id, label HAVING duplicate_count > 1 ORDER BY duplicate_count DESC, tenant_id ASC) AS d ON c.tenant_id = d.tenant_id AND c.label = d.label) AS targets ON r.catalog_id = targets.catalog_id SET r.repaired_label = CONCAT(targets.label, '-', r.catalog_id)

checks.sql: SELECT catalog_id, tenant_id, label, repaired_label FROM catalog_rows_min ORDER BY catalog_id
